title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas & Andrew Hunt
description: A comprehensive guide to software development practices and principles.
personalNotes: Essential reading for any developer. The concepts around DRY, orthogonality, and code generation have shaped how I approach software architecture.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
description: Rules for focused success in a distracted world.
personalNotes: Completely changed my approach to focus and concentration. The idea of treating deep work as a skill to be developed rather than something that just happens was revolutionary for my research workflow.

title: The Design of Everyday Things
author: Don Norman
description: The ultimate guide to human-centered design.
personalNotes: Fundamentally changed how I think about interfaces - both digital and physical. The concepts of affordances and signifiers are now part of my everyday vocabulary when building user experiences.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: Understanding the two systems that drive the way we think.
personalNotes: Incredible insights into cognitive biases and decision-making. Particularly relevant to my research on behavioral patterns in animals - many of the same cognitive shortcuts appear across species.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: An easy and proven way to build good habits and break bad ones.
personalNotes: Currently working through implementing the habit stacking concepts in my daily research routine. The 1% better every day philosophy aligns well with long-term research projects.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
description: Timeless lessons on wealth, greed, and happiness.
personalNotes: On my reading list because several colleagues have recommended it for understanding the behavioral aspects of financial decision-making.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship.
personalNotes: Essential for improving code quality and maintainability. Planning to read this to level up my software engineering practices.

title: Superintelligence
author: Nick Bostrom
description: Paths, dangers, strategies for artificial general intelligence.
personalNotes: Fascinating exploration of AI alignment and safety. Particularly relevant given the current advances in machine learning and their potential implications for society.
